subject: Manabe et al. (1982)
object: Manabe et al. (1982) described a female infant with congenital refractory sideroblastic anemia that did not respond to pyridoxine therapy.

subject: Manabe et al. (1982)
object: Manabe et al. (1982) found markedly reduced delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) synthetase activity in erythroblasts from the patient, both with and without pyridoxal phosphate treatment. Activity of erythroblast mitochondrial neutral protease, which specifically inactivates the apo form of ALA synthetase, was normal, and the apoenzyme's sensitivity to the protease was also normal. The authors speculated that the reduced ALA synthetase activity resulted from impaired production of the enzyme rather than faster breakdown, which could explain why the patient did not respond to pyridoxine.

subject: Jardine et al. (1994)
object: Jardine et al. (1994) reported a brother and sister, born to unaffected parents, who had transfusion-dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anemia from birth. Their hemoglobin levels were 4.3 and 6.4 g/dl, respectively.

subject: Jardine et al. (1994)
object: Jardine et al. (1994) found that delta-aminolevulinate synthase activity in erythroblasts from fractionated marrow of the affected sister was 135 pmol ALA formed/10(6) erythroblasts/hour, within the normal range of 110-650 pmol.

subject: Jardine et al. (1994)
object: In the affected son, Jardine et al. (1994) found no mutations in the ALAS2 gene on sequence analysis of the coding region, the intron/exon boundaries, or the 1-kb 5-prime promoter region.

subject: Jardine et al. (1994)
object: Jardine et al. (1994) identified a G-to-A polymorphism 220 nt 3-prime of the AATAAA polyadenylation signal of ALAS2, with a gene frequency of 25% in 148 alleles. Analysis of this intragenic polymorphism showed that the affected sibs had received different maternal alleles at the ALAS2 locus, which excluded ALAS2 mutations as the cause of their sideroblastic anemia.

subject: Jardine et al. (1994)
object: Jardine et al. (1994) found that the mother of the affected sibs had no dimorphic erythrocyte population and showed random X inactivation in peripheral leukocytes, which indicated that she did not carry an X-linked sideroblastic anemia mutation. The authors concluded that the results strongly suggested autosomal recessive inheritance in this family.

subject: Guernsey et al. (2009)
object: By positional cloning, Guernsey et al. (2009) identified mutations in the SLC25A38 gene, which encodes an erythroid-specific mitochondrial carrier family protein, in patients with a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia.

subject: Guernsey et al. (2009)
object: Guernsey et al. (2009) noted that the sideroblastic anemias are a heterogeneous group of congenital and acquired hematologic disorders whose morphologic hallmark is the presence of ringed sideroblasts, bone marrow erythroid precursors containing pathologic iron deposits within mitochondria.

subject: Guernsey et al. (2009)
object: Guernsey et al. (2009) demonstrated that SLC25A38 is important for the biosynthesis of heme in eukaryotes.

subject: ANEMIA, SIDEROBLASTIC, 2, PYRIDOXINE-REFRACTORY
object: Elevated bone marrow ring sideroblast count
